newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut's Solidere at new highs.
newsitem.headline: Beirut's Solidere at new highs.

text.p: Solidere shares steamed ahead to their highest level in two years in strong demand on the Beirut Stock Exchange, rising 4.7 percent to $13.75 on Tuesday.
The LIBX bank index rose 0.40 percent to 181.01. The BLOM general index climbed 3.85 percent to hit a record 1160.09. The LISPI general index increased 0.96 percent to hit 95.71.
Market turnover rose to 444,581 shares for a value of $6,179,930 against Monday's 306,783 shares for a value of $3,914,873.
Solidere dominated market activity with turnover of 388,971 shares for a value of $5,348,351.
Both Solidere A and B rose to $13.75 from $13.1250. The shares continued trading in strong demand.
"There is a lot of demand from Arab countries. A lot of orders are not being executed while all supply is being bought," a broker, who wished not to be identified said.
Demand for Solidere A shares on the first fixing was 686,787 against a supply of 225,273 shares while demand on the first fixing for B shares was 332,136 against 49,769 in supply.
Last Thursday's news that Solidere planned to open up share ownership to foreign investors in October fuelled a surge by the company's shares.
Bank of Beirut maintained it $4.625 record high while Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce rose to $20.75 from $20.5.
There was no trade in the four listed industrial firms: Ciment Libanaise, Ciments Blanc, Eternit and Uniceramic.
